- User is working during those hours (9-5 on weekends)
- Son is user's child, so primary responsibility for transportation falls to user... but it's reasonable to ask for help from a partner, especially one who's " in and out of each其他 homes" and has a car.

"Part of this family" implies a level of commitment he may not have agreed to. "Wouldn't mind doing small stuff" minimizes the ask - but for someone who's not a co-parent, it's not " small stuff" if it's not his child. 

Also, the boyfriend's perspective: 
- He works 7am-7pm weekdays (12-hour shifts)
- User extended her own work hours to afford football (so she's already working more)
- He's saying " I'm working longer hours to support me and my son" - wait, that's not accurate. User extended her hours, not him. He's probably feeling overburdened by the expectation to be a de facto co-parent without being one. 

The " I'm working longer hours to support you" claim is... odd. If user extended her own hours, he's not supporting her financially by working longer. Unless... did he? The scenario doesn't say. But user said " I extended my hours at work to afford it" - so it's her own choice. 

Then he says " I wanted to use weekends to go to football games etc as I wasn't at home anyway" - meaning he's not around much, so he wants personal time. 

The real issue: 
- User is treating the boyfriend as a co-parent without having established that dynamic. 
- " Part of this family" is a huge leap for a 3-year relationship where they don't live together. 
- The ask itself (transportation) is reasonable... but the framing was demanding and guilt-trippy. 
- Boyfriend's reaction ( breakup suggestion) is harsh, but his frustration is valid - he's being asked to承担 responsibilities of a parent without the relationship status to match.

- User: for framing it as " part of this family" and " wouldn't mind doing small stuff" - that's putting pressure on him to be more than a boyfriend. 
- Boyfriend: for suggesting breakup over this, and for going to the mum ( though that's less about being an asshole and more about being immature).
